summary: Use bounded non-swappable RAM for the standby courier's temporary SQLite snapshots while preserving the scheduled transfer and receiver integrity checks.

verification.observed: PR687 head bd9c9640c1047e8bd83aa73c5cb712fb92e374e7 passed both primary checks, merged as 5da314fa69b5a626964a48d342f747d87f8c216f, and merged-main pipeline 2422 passed. Twenty focused courier, receiver, and drill tests passed independently.

On the existing builder-to-source SSH and sudo route, an isolated systemd unit verified a 512 MiB noswap tmpfs, 768 MiB memory cap and zero swap allowance, then copied and restored a synthetic SQLite database. The fixture was removed and the host /tmp mount remained ext4.

At 07:04:23 UTC the sender changed from SHA256 5c9a20c5aa0ea033512adfba7e151bbb243b15c7133cc19aca174651ddaff314 to 0d3350ec6f4bb67a370d6a9ad4908780c616f4e096119500f269154e6cc52bc9 under the existing courier flock. A root-private before-image was retained; service and timer were not restarted.

The 07:05 and 07:07 UTC scheduled runs exited successfully. The receiver reported successful SQLite integrity and nonempty-table checks for both databases; both standby last-sync timestamps advanced, the timer stayed active, and the textfile success metric was 1.

A 135-second baseline and post-install window observed guest block writes of 494264320 and 169340928 bytes respectively. The old courier created two new disk scratch files totalling 339894272 logical bytes; the updated courier created none. The windows included other concurrent work.

limitations: Guest block and cgroup counters overlap and do not measure physical NAND writes; one comparison does not prove a sustained daily or fleet-wide reduction.
The private scratch filesystem is capped at 512 MiB and a source database above 448 MiB or low available memory stops that snapshot; existing standby-sync alerts remain the failure signal.

Scoped release metadata follows the documented WS0514 workflow. The previous global release manager refused unrelated active workstreams and waiver blockers before mutation; this receipt makes no global readiness claim.
